name: Barcode Scanner
tagline: A text field with a device barcode/QR scan button.

limitations: The scan is simulated. On the Power Apps mobile app, Scan opens the device's own scanner; the demo has no camera to reach, so the On the mobile app preset answers context.device.getBarcodeValue() with a fixed code, 9780201633610, and the event log under the demo says the answer was simulated. What the control does with it is real: the code lands in the field and in the value output a form would save.

The In a desktop browser preset declares no scanner, so getBarcodeValue() is refused and Scan shows the control's own "Scanning isn't available here" state; typing the code in still fills the field, since that path never touches context.device. A model-driven form in a desktop browser has no getBarcodeValue either — but this control declares Device.getBarcodeValue as required, so what such a form does with it, show this state or not load the control, is unmeasured.

presets.name: On the mobile app
presets.description: An empty field on the Power Apps mobile app. Press Scan: the demo answers as the device's scanner would, with a simulated EAN-13, and the code lands in the field.

presets.name: In a desktop browser
presets.description: The same empty field where there is no scanner to call. Scan shows the control's no-scanner state, and typing the code in still works.

presets.name: Already scanned
presets.description: Shows the field's post-scan state without needing a working scanner.
